metadata.source_policy: Answer only from retrieved source-grounded chunks. Do not invent missing BIS requirements. Use the latest source represented in the database where revision information is available.

answer_rules: Answer the user's actual question, not the most similar sentence.
If the user asks for a standard, begin with the IS number and title.
If the user asks how to apply, give a short ordered process using application/process chunks.
If the user asks about labs, use laboratory chunks and identify the BIS LIMS route when supported.
If the user asks about tests, summarize relevant tests instead of copying a database paragraph.
Answer in the same language as the user when possible.
Do not expose chunk IDs, embeddings, RAG terminology, or internal retrieval details.
Cite the supporting BIS source document and location.
If evidence is insufficient, clearly say it could not be verified from the available BIS sources.

metadata.design_note: Source-grounded retrieval database. The assistant must synthesize answers from retrieved chunks and never dump chunk text verbatim.

chunks.content: IS 14543:2024 is the third revision for Packaged Drinking Water (other than Packaged Natural Mineral Water). It was issued in March 2024 and is associated with ICS 13.060.20.
chunks.answer_instruction: Use this chunk as evidence. Do not copy it verbatim. Synthesize only the facts needed to answer the user's question.

chunks.content: Products conforming to IS 14543:2024 may be certified under the applicable BIS conformity-assessment scheme and may be marked with the Standard Mark, subject to applicable BIS requirements.
chunks.answer_instruction: Use this chunk as evidence. Do not copy it verbatim. Synthesize only the facts needed to answer the user's question.

chunks.content: The maximum colour requirement for packaged drinking water is 2 true colour units.
chunks.answer_instruction: Use this chunk as evidence. Do not copy it verbatim. Synthesize only the facts needed to answer the user's question.

chunks.content: The odour of packaged drinking water shall be agreeable.
chunks.answer_instruction: Use this chunk as evidence. Do not copy it verbatim. Synthesize only the facts needed to answer the user's question.

chunks.content: The taste of packaged drinking water shall be agreeable, assessed using the specified action tendency scale.
chunks.answer_instruction: Use this chunk as evidence. Do not copy it verbatim. Synthesize only the facts needed to answer the user's question.

chunks.content: The maximum turbidity requirement is 2 NTU.
chunks.answer_instruction: Use this chunk as evidence. Do not copy it verbatim. Synthesize only the facts needed to answer the user's question.

chunks.content: The maximum total dissolved solids (TDS) requirement is 500 mg/l.
chunks.answer_instruction: Use this chunk as evidence. Do not copy it verbatim. Synthesize only the facts needed to answer the user's question.

chunks.content: The pH requirement for packaged drinking water is 6.0 to 8.5.
chunks.answer_instruction: Use this chunk as evidence. Do not copy it verbatim. Synthesize only the facts needed to answer the user's question.

chunks.content: The maximum nitrate (as NO3) requirement is 45 mg/l.
chunks.answer_instruction: Use this chunk as evidence. Do not copy it verbatim. Synthesize only the facts needed to answer the user's question.

chunks.content: The maximum nitrite (as NO2) requirement is 0.02 mg/l.
chunks.answer_instruction: Use this chunk as evidence. Do not copy it verbatim. Synthesize only the facts needed to answer the user's question.

chunks.content: The maximum fluoride (as F) requirement is 1.0 mg/l.
chunks.answer_instruction: Use this chunk as evidence. Do not copy it verbatim. Synthesize only the facts needed to answer the user's question.

chunks.content: The standard specifies requirements for toxic substances and other chemical parameters; the assistant should retrieve the specific parameter chunk before giving a numerical limit.
chunks.answer_instruction: Use this chunk as evidence. Do not copy it verbatim. Synthesize only the facts needed to answer the user's question.

chunks.content: IS 14543:2024 references methods from the IS 3025 series and other referenced standards for determining specified characteristics. Approved and validated international methods may also be followed where permitted, with the specified reference methods applying in case of dispute.
chunks.answer_instruction: Use this chunk as evidence. Do not copy it verbatim. Synthesize only the facts needed to answer the user's question.

chunks.content: Nitrate may be determined using IS 3025 (Part 34/Sec 1) or IS 3025 (Part 75), as specified in the Product Manual's testing information.
chunks.source_location: Test equipment and test-method information, page 15; Scheme of Inspection and Testing, page 35
chunks.answer_instruction: Use this chunk as evidence. Do not copy it verbatim. Synthesize only the facts needed to answer the user's question.

chunks.content: Nitrate (as NO3) is tested on one sample once in a week under the levels of control in the Product Manual's Scheme of Inspection and Testing.
chunks.answer_instruction: Use this chunk as evidence. Do not copy it verbatim. Synthesize only the facts needed to answer the user's question.

chunks.content: The Product Manual specifies microbiological testing frequencies by parameter. Several parameters are tested on one sample from each control unit, while faecal streptococci/Staphylococcus aureus, Salmonella/Shigella, and specified Vibrio organisms have monthly frequencies.
chunks.answer_instruction: Use this chunk as evidence. Do not copy it verbatim. Synthesize only the facts needed to answer the user's question.

chunks.content: Colour, odour, taste, turbidity and total dissolved solids are specified as one sample from each control unit in the levels of control. The pH entry requires adequate inspections and in-process controls to ensure conformity.
chunks.answer_instruction: Use this chunk as evidence. Do not copy it verbatim. Synthesize only the facts needed to answer the user's question.

chunks.content: The Scheme of Inspection and Testing specifies different frequencies for chemical parameters. Examples include barium, copper, iron and manganese monthly; nitrate, nitrite and aluminium weekly; fluoride and selenium six-monthly; and chloride, sulphate, alkalinity and residual free chlorine for each control unit.
chunks.answer_instruction: Use this chunk as evidence. Do not copy it verbatim. Synthesize only the facts needed to answer the user's question.

chunks.content: PM/14543/7, July 2025, is reference material for BIS Regional/Branch Offices and licensees for certification under Scheme-I and may also be used by prospective applicants seeking BIS certification.
chunks.answer_instruction: Use this chunk as evidence. Do not copy it verbatim. Synthesize only the facts needed to answer the user's question.

chunks.content: Domestic manufacturers of packaged drinking water apply online through the Manakonline system using Form V as specified in Scheme I of Schedule II of the BIS Conformity Assessment Regulations, 2018.
chunks.answer_instruction: Use this chunk as evidence. Do not copy it verbatim. Synthesize only the facts needed to answer the user's question.

chunks.content: For the normal procedure, after the application is received and found complete, BIS visits the applicant's factory to assess manufacturing infrastructure, production process, quality control and testing capabilities, hygiene conditions, and to draw samples for third-party laboratory testing.
chunks.answer_instruction: Use this chunk as evidence. Do not copy it verbatim. Synthesize only the facts needed to answer the user's question.

chunks.content: During preliminary inspection, one product sample is tested in the factory for specified requirements including description, colour, odour, taste, turbidity, TDS, pH, chloride, alkalinity and residual free chlorine.
chunks.answer_instruction: Use this chunk as evidence. Do not copy it verbatim. Synthesize only the facts needed to answer the user's question.

chunks.content: If the factory sample passes the specified factory testing, a packaged drinking water sample is drawn and sent for complete testing for all requirements of the Indian Standard in a third-party laboratory.
chunks.answer_instruction: Use this chunk as evidence. Do not copy it verbatim. Synthesize only the facts needed to answer the user's question.

chunks.content: A source-grounded certification flow for domestic manufacturers is: submit the application online through Manakonline; BIS assesses the application and conducts a factory visit under the normal procedure; manufacturing, quality-control, testing and hygiene capabilities are assessed; factory testing is performed; if the sample passes, samples are sent for complete third-party laboratory testing; applicable BIS certification procedures under Scheme-I are then followed.
chunks.answer_instruction: Use this chunk as evidence. Do not copy it verbatim. Synthesize only the facts needed to answer the user's question.

chunks.content: The hygiene requirements cover facility location, drainage, waste disposal, pest prevention, lighting, ventilation, raw-water handling, cleaning and sanitation of water-contact surfaces, packaging hygiene, storage, traceability and transport cleanliness.
chunks.answer_instruction: Use this chunk as evidence. Do not copy it verbatim. Synthesize only the facts needed to answer the user's question.

chunks.content: Packaged drinking water certification surveillance includes visits at the factory, including testing of samples drawn from the factory, and drawing samples from the market for third-party laboratory testing.
chunks.answer_instruction: Use this chunk as evidence. Do not copy it verbatim. Synthesize only the facts needed to answer the user's question.

chunks.content: The source of water must be identified. During inspection, changes in source of water are checked and reported. The Product Manual also requires source-water testing at specified intervals and notification, testing and approval when the source changes.
chunks.source_location: Annex A and Scheme of Inspection and Testing
chunks.answer_instruction: Use this chunk as evidence. Do not copy it verbatim. Synthesize only the facts needed to answer the user's question.

chunks.content: The scheme requires records and controls for production, testing, marking and dispatch, supporting traceability and verification during BIS inspections.
chunks.answer_instruction: Use this chunk as evidence. Do not copy it verbatim. Synthesize only the facts needed to answer the user's question.

chunks.content: The licence scope covers Packaged Drinking Water other than Packaged Natural Mineral Water and specifies varieties based on packaging type and container material.
chunks.answer_instruction: Use this chunk as evidence. Do not copy it verbatim. Synthesize only the facts needed to answer the user's question.

chunks.topic: How to apply for BIS certification
chunks.content: For domestic manufacturers seeking BIS certification for packaged drinking water under IS 14543:2024, the Product Manual states that applications are submitted online through Manakonline using Form V under Scheme-I. The application is accepted under Option 1 (Normal procedure).
chunks.answer_instruction: Use this chunk as evidence. Do not copy it verbatim. Synthesize only the facts needed to answer the user's question.
chunks.topic_group: How to apply for BIS certification

chunks.content: BIS product certification applications are accepted through the online Manakonline portal. BIS states that applicants should first identify the applicable Indian Standard and then analyse and document the required manufacturing infrastructure, process controls, quality control and testing capabilities.
chunks.answer_instruction: Use this chunk as evidence. Do not copy it verbatim. Synthesize only the facts needed to answer the user's question.

chunks.content: Before applying, the manufacturer should have the required manufacturing infrastructure, appropriate process controls, quality control and testing capabilities for the product according to the applicable Indian Standard.
chunks.source_location: Steps to be followed for applying for a licence
chunks.answer_instruction: Use this chunk as evidence. Do not copy it verbatim. Synthesize only the facts needed to answer the user's question.

chunks.content: The BIS Grant of Licence guidelines specify documents and information to be verified during the factory visit. These include the self-evaluation cum verification report, quality control personnel details, calibration certificates of testing equipment, applicable raw-material test certificates, product/component samples, hygienic-condition report where applicable, plant layout, factory location plan, information about subcontracted testing, and the proposed quality assurance or inspection and test plan where applicable.
chunks.source_document: BIS Guidelines for Grant of Licence
chunks.answer_instruction: Use this chunk as evidence. Do not copy it verbatim. Synthesize only the facts needed to answer the user's question.

chunks.content: The self-evaluation cum verification report includes general information about the applicant, plant layout, other premises involved in manufacturing where applicable, raw materials and suppliers, supplier test certificates, packing and marking information, previous BIS certification details where applicable, quality-control staff details, and brand name or trademark information.
chunks.source_document: BIS Guidelines for Grant of Licence
chunks.answer_instruction: Use this chunk as evidence. Do not copy it verbatim. Synthesize only the facts needed to answer the user's question.

chunks.content: The Grant of Licence guidelines require details of quality control personnel to be verified during the factory visit. The self-evaluation report records the name, designation, qualification and experience of quality-control staff.
chunks.source_document: BIS Guidelines for Grant of Licence
chunks.answer_instruction: Use this chunk as evidence. Do not copy it verbatim. Synthesize only the facts needed to answer the user's question.

chunks.content: Calibration certificates for testing equipment are among the documents verified during the BIS factory visit, as applicable.
chunks.source_document: BIS Guidelines for Grant of Licence
chunks.answer_instruction: Use this chunk as evidence. Do not copy it verbatim. Synthesize only the facts needed to answer the user's question.

chunks.content: Copies of test certificates for raw materials are verified during the factory visit where applicable. The self-evaluation report also records raw materials used, supplier information and supplier test-certificate information.
chunks.source_document: BIS Guidelines for Grant of Licence
chunks.answer_instruction: Use this chunk as evidence. Do not copy it verbatim. Synthesize only the facts needed to answer the user's question.

chunks.content: The BIS factory visit requirements include verification of a plant layout showing relevant manufacturing, storage and testing areas and a location plan of the factory.
chunks.source_document: BIS Guidelines for Grant of Licence
chunks.answer_instruction: Use this chunk as evidence. Do not copy it verbatim. Synthesize only the facts needed to answer the user's question.

chunks.content: For packaged drinking water, the Product Manual requires the submitted factory layout to identify relevant areas including the raw-water source and entry point, raw-water storage, production stages, filling and packing areas, laboratory, storage areas and factory boundary.
chunks.answer_instruction: Use this chunk as evidence. Do not copy it verbatim. Synthesize only the facts needed to answer the user's question.

chunks.content: After a complete application is received under the normal procedure, BIS visits the applicant's factory. The visit assesses manufacturing infrastructure, production process, quality control and testing capabilities, hygiene conditions and includes drawing samples for third-party laboratory testing.
chunks.answer_instruction: Use this chunk as evidence. Do not copy it verbatim. Synthesize only the facts needed to answer the user's question.

chunks.content: During preliminary inspection for packaged drinking water, factory testing includes specified requirements such as description, colour, odour, taste, turbidity, TDS, pH, chloride, alkalinity and residual free chlorine.
chunks.answer_instruction: Use this chunk as evidence. Do not copy it verbatim. Synthesize only the facts needed to answer the user's question.

chunks.content: If factory testing passes as specified in the Product Manual, the sample is sent for complete testing against the requirements of the Indian Standard at a third-party laboratory.
chunks.answer_instruction: Use this chunk as evidence. Do not copy it verbatim. Synthesize only the facts needed to answer the user's question.

chunks.content: BIS grants a product certification licence based on successful assessment of manufacturing infrastructure, process controls, quality control and testing capabilities. Conformity of the product is established through applicable testing at the manufacturing premises, third-party laboratory testing, or a combination as specified by BIS.
chunks.answer_instruction: Use this chunk as evidence. Do not copy it verbatim. Synthesize only the facts needed to answer the user's question.

chunks.content: For a BIS Scheme-I application, documents and information that may need to be verified include the self-evaluation cum verification report, quality control personnel details, calibration certificates, applicable raw-material test certificates, product samples, hygienic-condition report where applicable, plant layout, factory location plan, subcontracted testing information where applicable, and the applicable quality assurance or inspection and test plan.
chunks.source_document: BIS Guidelines for Grant of Licence
chunks.answer_instruction: Use this chunk as evidence. Do not copy it verbatim. Synthesize only the facts needed to answer the user's question.

chunks.content: BIS states that applicants should refer to the applicable fee information for application, inspection and annual licence fees. Product-specific marking fees may also apply. The exact current fee should be checked from the official BIS fee information rather than inferred from this dataset.
chunks.answer_instruction: Use this chunk as evidence. Do not copy it verbatim. Synthesize only the facts needed to answer the user's question.

chunks.content: BIS states that applications for product certification are accepted only through online mode, including payments, through the Manakonline portal.
chunks.answer_instruction: Use this chunk as evidence. Do not copy it verbatim. Synthesize only the facts needed to answer the user's question.

chunks.content: IS 13428:2024 is the Indian Standard titled 'Packaged Natural Mineral Water — Specification' and is the Third Revision.
chunks.answer_instruction: Use this chunk as evidence. Do not copy it verbatim. Synthesize only the facts needed to answer the user's question.

chunks.content: The BIS Standard Details page for IS 13428:2024 lists the certification type as Voluntary Certification.
chunks.answer_instruction: Use this chunk as evidence. Do not copy it verbatim. Synthesize only the facts needed to answer the user's question.

chunks.content: IS 13428:2024 supersedes IS 13428:2005. The BIS Gazette notification states that IS 13428:2024 was established on 15 March 2024 and IS 13428:2005 was withdrawn on 15 September 2024.
chunks.answer_instruction: Use this chunk as evidence. Do not copy it verbatim. Synthesize only the facts needed to answer the user's question.

chunks.content: Domestic manufacturers of packaged natural mineral water shall apply for grant of licence online through the Manakonline system using Form V specified in Scheme I of Schedule II of the BIS (Conformity Assessment) Regulations, 2018.
chunks.answer_instruction: Use this chunk as evidence. Do not copy it verbatim. Synthesize only the facts needed to answer the user's question.

chunks.content: Applications are accepted under Option 1 (Normal procedure). After the application is received and found complete, BIS visits the applicant's factory to assess manufacturing infrastructure, production process, quality control and testing capabilities, hygiene conditions, and to draw a sample for testing in a third-party laboratory.
chunks.answer_instruction: Use this chunk as evidence. Do not copy it verbatim. Synthesize only the facts needed to answer the user's question.

chunks.content: The factory layout submitted with the application is verified during preliminary inspection. It should indicate the raw-water source and entry point, manufacturing plant and stages, filling/packing areas, change room and toilets, entry/exit arrangements, packaging and finished-product stores, laboratory, and establishment boundary.
chunks.answer_instruction: Use this chunk as evidence. Do not copy it verbatim. Synthesize only the facts needed to answer the user's question.

chunks.content: During preliminary inspection, production and filling/packing should be carried out as a trial batch so that the firm's capability can be assessed.
chunks.answer_instruction: Use this chunk as evidence. Do not copy it verbatim. Synthesize only the facts needed to answer the user's question.

chunks.content: Availability of manufacturing facilities, including filling and/or packaging machinery for the varieties applied for, is verified during preliminary inspection.
chunks.answer_instruction: Use this chunk as evidence. Do not copy it verbatim. Synthesize only the facts needed to answer the user's question.

chunks.content: Compliance with hygienic practices is verified during inspection using the product manual's Hygiene Checklist. The manual states that the checklist is verified, filled, signed and uploaded with the Factory Test Report, and hygiene assessment is performed during preliminary, surveillance and verification inspections.
chunks.answer_instruction: Use this chunk as evidence. Do not copy it verbatim. Synthesize only the facts needed to answer the user's question.

chunks.content: The product manual describes natural mineral water as water obtained directly from natural or drilled underground water-bearing sources, characterized by mineral composition and trace constituents, with constancy of composition and stability of discharge and temperature, collected under conditions preserving original microbiological purity and essential chemical composition, packaged close to the point of emergence with hygienic precautions, and not subjected to treatments other than those permitted by the standard.
chunks.answer_instruction: Use this chunk as evidence. Do not copy it verbatim. Synthesize only the facts needed to answer the user's question.

chunks.content: The product manual states that transport of natural mineral water in bulk containers for packaging or any other process before packaging is prohibited.
chunks.answer_instruction: Use this chunk as evidence. Do not copy it verbatim. Synthesize only the facts needed to answer the user's question.

chunks.content: Evidence for constancy of water composition at the source across seasonal fluctuations includes test reports from a BIS-approved outside laboratory for major seasons over one year for major physicochemical parameters, a manufacturer record of temperature at the discharge/emergence point, and a hydrogeologist report covering genesis, residence period, chemical, physical and radiological qualities, and pollution risk.
chunks.answer_instruction: Use this chunk as evidence. Do not copy it verbatim. Synthesize only the facts needed to answer the user's question.

chunks.content: Required testing facilities according to the Indian Standard and Scheme of Inspection and Testing are verified during inspection. Test equipment should have valid calibration on the day of the visit. Calibration should be from a NABL-accredited laboratory or another laboratory with traceability to NPL established through calibration certificates.
chunks.answer_instruction: Use this chunk as evidence. Do not copy it verbatim. Synthesize only the facts needed to answer the user's question.

chunks.content: Testing personnel qualifications, competence and experience are verified. The manual lists relevant science, engineering, chemistry, microbiology, biotechnology, biochemistry, food technology, botany and other biological/life-science backgrounds among the disciplines that may be engaged.
chunks.answer_instruction: Use this chunk as evidence. Do not copy it verbatim. Synthesize only the facts needed to answer the user's question.

chunks.content: During preliminary inspection, one product sample is tested in the factory for preferably Description, Colour, Odour, Taste, Turbidity, Total Dissolved Solids (TDS), pH, Chloride and Alkalinity.
chunks.answer_instruction: Use this chunk as evidence. Do not copy it verbatim. Synthesize only the facts needed to answer the user's question.

chunks.content: If the factory sample passes factory testing, a sample of natural mineral water is drawn and sent for testing for the requirements of the Indian Standard. The test request is generated through Manakonline.
chunks.answer_instruction: Use this chunk as evidence. Do not copy it verbatim. Synthesize only the facts needed to answer the user's question.

chunks.content: The test request for independent testing should specify, where applicable, whether the product is Natural Spring Water, date of manufacture/packing and batch number, expiry/use-by information, quantity of packaged water, type/material/capacity of containers, and declared wall thickness or pouch-film width.
chunks.answer_instruction: Use this chunk as evidence. Do not copy it verbatim. Synthesize only the facts needed to answer the user's question.

chunks.content: The licence scope is for use of the Standard Mark as per IS 13428:2024. The scope specifies the product name and packaging varieties, including packaging material, container type and capacity. Examples in the manual include PET bottles of 500 ml, 1 litre and 1.5 litre and/or PET jars of 20 litres.
chunks.answer_instruction: Use this chunk as evidence. Do not copy it verbatim. Synthesize only the facts needed to answer the user's question.

chunks.content: The Scheme of Inspection and Testing in the product manual specifies control frequencies for different parameters. Examples include nitrate, nitrite and sulphide once a week; manganese, copper and barium once a month; fluoride once in six months; radioactive alpha/beta emitters once in five years; pesticide residues once a year; and shelf-life assessment once in six months for each type of container.
chunks.source_location: Scheme of Inspection and Testing, Table 1
chunks.answer_instruction: Use this chunk as evidence. Do not copy it verbatim. Synthesize only the facts needed to answer the user's question.

chunks.content: The product manual contains separate surveillance guidelines under Annex-B. During periodic inspection, changes in manufacturing facilities, hygiene practices, source of water, treatment/disinfection processes, testing facilities, testing personnel and compliance with the Scheme of Inspection and Testing are checked.
chunks.answer_instruction: Use this chunk as evidence. Do not copy it verbatim. Synthesize only the facts needed to answer the user's question.

chunks.content: The product manual contains guidelines for action in case of non-conformity, including suspension and revocation of suspension, under Annex-C.
chunks.answer_instruction: Use this chunk as evidence. Do not copy it verbatim. Synthesize only the facts needed to answer the user's question.

chunks.content: The BIS Standard Details page for IS 13428:2024 lists 48 laboratories associated with the standard. Examples shown include ALS Testing Services India Pvt. Ltd., Bengaluru; Umwelt Research Lab Private Limited, Pune; Accurate Universal Laboratories Private Limited, Ahmedabad; ADARSH SCIENTIFIC RESEARCH CENTER AND TESTING LABORATORY; Precise Analytics Lab.; and Eureka Analytical Services Private Limited, Bengaluru.
chunks.answer_instruction: Use this chunk as evidence. Do not copy it verbatim. Synthesize only the facts needed to answer the user's question.

chunks.content: The BIS Standard Details page lists Amendment 00, Gazette Document 01, Licence 17, Product Manual & SIT 01, Laboratory 48, Corrigendum 00, Summary 01, and Test Request & Report Format 00.
chunks.answer_instruction: Use this chunk as evidence. Do not copy it verbatim. Synthesize only the facts needed to answer the user's question.

chunks.content: The supplied BIS summary describes IS 13428:2024 as addressing microbiological, chemical and radiological quality parameters, safe and hygienic packaging, preservation of natural mineral composition, regular testing and quality audits.
chunks.answer_instruction: Use this chunk as evidence. Do not copy it verbatim. Synthesize only the facts needed to answer the user's question.

chunks.content: BIS Product Manual PM/9873/12 is reference material for certification under Scheme-I of the BIS (Conformity Assessment) Regulations, 2018 and may be used by prospective applicants seeking a BIS certification licence.
chunks.source_document: Product Manual for Safety of Toys
chunks.answer_instruction: Use this chunk as evidence. Do not copy it verbatim. Synthesize only the facts needed to answer the user's question.

chunks.content: The manual lists IS 9873 Part 1:2019 mechanical and physical properties; Part 2:2017 flammability; Part 3:2020 migration of certain elements; Part 4:2017 swings, slides and similar activity toys; Part 7:2017 finger paints; Part 9:2017 certain phthalate esters; and IS 15644:2006 safety of electric toys.
chunks.answer_instruction: Use this chunk as evidence. Do not copy it verbatim. Synthesize only the facts needed to answer the user's question.

chunks.content: The supplied BIS Gazette notification states that IS 9873 (Part 1):2025, ISO 8124-1:2022, Safety of Toys Part 1, was established on 23 September 2025 and IS 9873 (Part 1):2019 was to be withdrawn on 23 March 2026.
chunks.answer_instruction: Use this chunk as evidence. Do not copy it verbatim. Synthesize only the facts needed to answer the user's question.

chunks.content: The supplied BIS Gazette notification states that IS 9873 (Part 2):2025, ISO 8124-2:2023, Safety of Toys Part 2 Flammability, was established on 23 September 2025 and IS 9873 (Part 2):2017 was to be withdrawn on 23 March 2026.
chunks.answer_instruction: Use this chunk as evidence. Do not copy it verbatim. Synthesize only the facts needed to answer the user's question.

chunks.content: The supplied BIS Gazette notification states that IS 9873 (Part 6):2025, ISO 8124-6:2023, Safety of Toys Part 6 Certain Phthalate Esters, was established on 23 September 2025 and IS 9873 (Part 6):2021 was to be withdrawn on 23 March 2026.
chunks.answer_instruction: Use this chunk as evidence. Do not copy it verbatim. Synthesize only the facts needed to answer the user's question.

chunks.content: The supplied BIS Standard Details snapshot identifies IS 9873 (Part 1):2019, ISO 8124-1:2018, Safety of Toys Part 1: Safety Aspects Related to Mechanical and Physical Properties, reviewed in 2025. It shows Certification: N/A and lists 2 Gazette Documents, 1272 licences, 1 Product Manual & SIT, 25 laboratories, 1 corrigendum and 1 summary.
chunks.answer_instruction: Use this chunk as evidence. Do not copy it verbatim. Synthesize only the facts needed to answer the user's question.

chunks.content: For raw-material sampling guidance, all materials shall be visually clean and free from infestation, assessed by normal corrected vision rather than magnification, with reference to Clause 4.3 of IS 9873 Part 1:2019 in the supplied manual.
chunks.answer_instruction: Use this chunk as evidence. Do not copy it verbatim. Synthesize only the facts needed to answer the user's question.

chunks.content: The product manual specifies a sample size of 3 to 10 pieces. Depending on toy size, the certification officer consults the laboratory to ensure sufficient quantity for complete testing. Samples are to be fully packaged and labelled.
chunks.answer_instruction: Use this chunk as evidence. Do not copy it verbatim. Synthesize only the facts needed to answer the user's question.

chunks.content: For certification, toys are classified into two types: Non-electric Toys, for which IS 9873 Part 1 is the primary standard and Parts 2, 3, 4, 7 and 9 are applicable secondary standards; and Electric Toys, for which IS 15644 is primary and IS 9873 Parts 1, 2, 3, 4, 7 and 9 are applicable secondary standards.
chunks.answer_instruction: Use this chunk as evidence. Do not copy it verbatim. Synthesize only the facts needed to answer the user's question.

chunks.content: The manual states that toys are further classified into 7 categories and 146 sub-categories based on specific purpose and function, using IS 9873 Part 8:2019 as the basis for classification.
chunks.answer_instruction: Use this chunk as evidence. Do not copy it verbatim. Synthesize only the facts needed to answer the user's question.

chunks.content: Varieties of toys of similar design, made from the same materials and covered under a single sub-category are considered a series for certification.
chunks.answer_instruction: Use this chunk as evidence. Do not copy it verbatim. Synthesize only the facts needed to answer the user's question.

chunks.content: For non-electric toys, a sample of the required quantity from any one model among models in the same series is drawn and tested for Grant of Licence or Change in Scope of Licence when the models have the same type, similar design, same materials and a single sub-category.
chunks.answer_instruction: Use this chunk as evidence. Do not copy it verbatim. Synthesize only the facts needed to answer the user's question.

chunks.content: Electric toys are grouped by input source into battery-operated, transformer and dual-supply toys. One representative model may be drawn for a series when the specified power layout, chassis/enclosure, power or battery characteristics, processor/controller and other applicable parameters are the same.
chunks.answer_instruction: Use this chunk as evidence. Do not copy it verbatim. Synthesize only the facts needed to answer the user's question.

chunks.content: Manufacturers applying for Grant of Licence submit a declaration/request in the Appendix II format to BIS through Manakonline. BIS assesses the application and defines the licence scope based on the submission.
chunks.answer_instruction: Use this chunk as evidence. Do not copy it verbatim. Synthesize only the facts needed to answer the user's question.

chunks.content: The Appendix II declaration asks for toy type, description, category, sub-category, electric input source where applicable, starting age, series number and primary/secondary applicable standards.

chunks.standard_title: Protective Helmet for Two Wheeler Riders
chunks.content: The 2020 Quality Control Order requires covered helmets to conform to IS 4151:2015 and bear the Standard Mark under a BIS licence according to Scheme-I. The order came into force on 1 June 2021.

chunks.standard_title: Protective Helmet for Two Wheeler Riders
chunks.content: BIS is the certifying and enforcing authority for the helmet product covered by the 2020 Quality Control Order.

chunks.standard_title: Protective Helmet for Two Wheeler Riders
chunks.content: The IS 4151 product manual is reference material for BIS offices and licensees and may also be used by prospective applicants seeking BIS certification. Certification under this product manual is operated under Scheme-I.

chunks.standard_title: Protective Helmet for Two Wheeler Riders
chunks.content: The product manual states that a licence to use the Standard Mark under IS 4151:2015 has a defined scope covering the protective helmet product, including model/design, type and size.

chunks.standard_title: Protective Helmet for Two Wheeler Riders
chunks.content: For licence coverage, a helmet of each model/design, type and size is to be tested to cover that variety in the licence.

chunks.standard_title: Protective Helmet for Two Wheeler Riders
chunks.content: The December 2024 BIS product manual specifies a sample quantity of 9 helmets plus 3 metres of chin strap.

chunks.standard_title: Protective Helmet for Two Wheeler Riders
chunks.content: Possible tests listed by the product manual include size, constructional requirements, peripheral vision, workmanship and finish, mass, and dynamic testing of the retention system.
chunks.source_location: Page 2, Possible Tests in a Day

chunks.standard_title: Protective Helmet for Two Wheeler Riders
chunks.content: The product manual covers impact absorption, rigidity, projections and surface friction, dynamic retention, audibility, retention/detaching, chin-strap micro-slip, chin-strap abrasion, and quick-release retention mechanisms where applicable.
chunks.source_location: Pages 3–10, Annex A and Annex B

chunks.standard_title: Protective Helmet for Two Wheeler Riders
chunks.content: Manufacturers/licensees are expected to have a suitably equipped and staffed in-house laboratory for parameters requiring routine testing and factory-level controls.

chunks.standard_title: Protective Helmet for Two Wheeler Riders
chunks.content: Tests permitted to be subcontracted may be carried out through a BIS-recognized/empanelled laboratory or another laboratory with valid NABL accreditation to IS/ISO/IEC 17025.

chunks.standard_title: Protective Helmet for Two Wheeler Riders
chunks.content: Test records for conformity testing are to be maintained. For subcontracted testing, laboratory test reports are to be available for inspection by BIS.

chunks.standard_title: Protective Helmet for Two Wheeler Riders
chunks.content: The Standard Mark specified in the licence schedule is to be clearly and indelibly marked on each helmet, provided the marked product conforms to the specification.

chunks.standard_title: Protective Helmet for Two Wheeler Riders
chunks.content: Helmet marking is to follow Clause 9 of IS 4151:2015. The product manual also gives additional marking requirements and traceability information for visors when provided.

chunks.standard_title: Protective Helmet for Two Wheeler Riders
chunks.content: Manufacturers/licensees are expected to implement a Quality Assurance Plan covering regular testing and in-process controls so products bearing the Standard Mark conform to the Indian Standard.

chunks.standard_title: Protective Helmet for Two Wheeler Riders
chunks.content: For guidance, helmets of the same model/design, type and size manufactured under similar conditions in a day constitute a control unit.

chunks.standard_title: Protective Helmet for Two Wheeler Riders
chunks.content: Quality-control areas include shell, protective padding, comfort padding, retention system, metal parts, visor when provided, size, constructional requirements, peripheral vision, workmanship and finish, and mass.

chunks.standard_title: Protective Helmet for Two Wheeler Riders
chunks.content: Table 1 gives test-specific sample quantities and frequencies. Examples include eight samples for size testing per control unit, five samples for impact absorption for each shape and size once in three months, and one sample for dynamic retention testing per control unit.
